records.title: CAM: A Causality-Based Analysis Framework for Multi-agent Code Generation Systems
records.reason: CAM estimates which intermediate outputs in multi-agent code-generation systems causally affect correctness and demonstrates repair and feature-pruning applications. Evaluations span agent systems/backends and code datasets; the paper is an analysis framework, not an inference-cost optimization, and results depend on simulated errors and selected systems. Potential agent-token pruning is adjacent but not established as a serving improvement.

records.title: Expert-Data Alignment Governs Generation Quality in Decentralized Diffusion Models
records.reason: The paper studies decentralized diffusion-model denoising experts and finds sparse Top-2 routing gives better generation quality than full expert aggregation. Its domain is image diffusion and expert/data alignment, not LLM serving or inference cost.

records.title: CAPS: Unifying Attention, Recurrence, and Alignment in Transformer-based Time Series Forecasting
records.reason: CAPS combines clock weighting, prefix-product recurrence and softmax paths for time-series forecasting and reports linear-complexity results on temporal forecasting benchmarks. The evaluated task is time series, with no language-model inference or serving evaluation.

records.title: Asymptotic Semantic Collapse in Hierarchical Optimization
records.reason: The paper models semantic-state convergence in a closed multi-agent linguistic system using manifold projection dynamics. Its claims are theoretical/synthetic convergence properties, not a practical LLM inference, memory, or serving optimization.

records.title: Enhancing video captioning with contextual anchor-guided semantic modeling
records.reason: The publisher full text describes a contextual-anchor encoder and frame-level global aggregator for video captioning, evaluated on MSVD and MSR-VTT. It reports caption-quality gains; it does not address sparse-attention efficiency, long-context language models, or serving.
